topline.text: Another quiet 24-48 hours - across DfE, Ofsted, safeguarding, funding and Sheffield/South Yorkshire sources, nothing cleared the bar for new, properly corroborated news, so today's edition runs short rather than padded.
Clock's ticking: DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform now closes in under two weeks (19 Nov).
Still pending: DfE's autumn 2025/26 suspensions and permanent exclusions statistics were due "this month" but no exact publication day has been confirmed yet.

diary.text: DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform (behaviour strategies, in-school units, managed moves) closes.
DfE due to publish autumn 2025/26 suspensions and permanent exclusions statistics for England.

items.lede: Exclusion reform call for evidence - under two weeks left to respond.
items.body: DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform, covering behaviour strategies, in-school units and managed moves, closes 19 November. It's seeking views from practitioners on reintegration barriers, parental engagement and what support works for different pupil groups - worth a look if the inclusion team wants its evidence reflected before it shuts.
items.action: Flag the 19 Nov deadline to the inclusion team now if a response is wanted.

box.label: Jargon-buster - in-school unit (ISU)
box.intro: One of the behaviour tools DfE's live exclusion-reform call for evidence is asking about.
box.text: A supervised space within a mainstream school - sometimes called a reintegration or support unit - where a pupil is placed for a fixed period, away from mainstream lessons, to manage behaviour before returning to class. It's used as a step short of suspension or exclusion.
